label: JZ Mock B · Paper 2 · Question 8
knowledgePattern: Audit sign conditions at each trigonometric inequality step
solution:
Line I subtracts the same cosine value from both sides and is valid. In II the quantity being squared is known to be positive; expansion and the sine/cosine squared identity are valid. III uses that identity again and correctly converts a strict square bound to an absolute-value bound.

In IV, the addition is valid up to sinθ>−1/2. But squaring this does not imply sin2θ>1/2: for example a sine value of zero satisfies the first inequality and fails the second. Thus IV is the first error: answer E.

The original premise itself allows this failure: at θ=π, sine is 0 and cosine is −1. The premise is true but the claimed conclusion is false. Line V would be valid if its two stated premises were available; the earlier invalid inference is the problem.

hints.title: Check what each operation assumes
hints.body: Audit the lines in order, recording the sign information available immediately before an addition, squaring or square-root step.
hints.recap: Each inference must follow from the assumptions and already justified lines.
hints.pitfall: A familiar-looking identity does not establish the sign needed for a different operation.
hints.pause: Decide whether every proposed inequality transformation has the conditions it needs.

hints.title: Test a doubtful implication locally
hints.body: For a step you cannot justify, try a simple value that satisfies its input inequality and check the output inequality.
hints.recap: The sign of a quantity matters when an inequality is transformed.
hints.pitfall: Rejecting the final conjecture alone does not identify where the first error occurred.
hints.pause: Identify the earliest unsupported step, and check a permitted trigonometric value if needed.
